aptitude.question: A manufacturing unit invests Rs. 20,000 in a fixed deposit at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. What is the compound interest earned at the end of 3 years?
A bonus pool of Rs. 84,000 is divided among three project teams in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. What is the largest share?
aptitude.explanation: Total parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. Largest share = 84,000 x 5/12 = Rs. 35,000.

aptitude.question: The average weight of 10 cartons in a shipment is 24 kg. When one carton is removed, the average weight of the remaining cartons becomes 23 kg. What is the weight of the carton that was removed?
aptitude.explanation: Total of 10 cartons = 10 x 24 = 240 kg. Total of 9 cartons = 9 x 23 = 207 kg. Removed carton = 240 - 207 = 33 kg.

aptitude.question: A storage tank can be filled by pipe A in 20 hours and by pipe B in 30 hours, while outlet pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 hours. All three pipes are opened together on an empty tank, and after 10 hours pipe C is closed. How many more hours will it take to fill the tank completely?
aptitude.explanation: Net rate with all three = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15 = (3 + 2 - 4)/60 = 1/60. In 10 hours: 10/60 = 1/6 filled. Remaining 5/6 at rate 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 per hour takes (5/6) x 12 = 10 hours.

aptitude.question: A cargo boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and 24 km upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
aptitude.explanation: Downstream speed = 36/3 = 12 km/h; upstream speed = 24/4 = 6 km/h. Stream speed = (12 - 6)/2 = 3 km/h.

aptitude.question: In a warehouse, 2/5 of the stock items are electronics, 1/3 of the remaining items are furniture, and the rest, 360 items, are stationery. How many stock items are there in total?
aptitude.explanation: After electronics, 3/5 remains. Furniture = 1/3 x 3/5 = 1/5. Stationery = 1 - 2/5 - 1/5 = 2/5 of total. So total = 360 / (2/5) = 900 items.

aptitude.question: A logistics firm hires 15 vehicles for a day, some vans at Rs. 1,200 per day and the rest trucks at Rs. 2,000 per day. The total hire charge is Rs. 22,000. How many trucks were hired?

A plant mixes two grades of lubricant costing Rs. 120 per litre and Rs. 180 per litre. In what ratio (cheaper : costlier) must they be mixed so that selling the mixture at Rs. 171.60 per litre gives a profit of 10%?
aptitude.explanation: Cost price of mixture = 171.60 / 1.10 = Rs. 156 per litre. By alligation, cheaper : costlier = (180 - 156) : (156 - 120) = 24 : 36 = 2 : 3.

aptitude.question: Find the next letter in the series: B, E, H, K, N, ?
aptitude.explanation: Each letter is 3 positions after the previous one: B(2), E(5), H(8), K(11), N(14), so the next is position 17 = Q.

aptitude.question: Which number is the odd one out? 144, 196, 250, 324
aptitude.explanation: 144 = 12^2, 196 = 14^2 and 324 = 18^2 are perfect squares. 250 is not a perfect square.

aptitude.question: Thermometer is to Temperature as Odometer is to ?
aptitude.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; an odometer measures the distance travelled by a vehicle. (Speed is measured by a speedometer.)

aptitude.question: In a certain code, BAD is written as 7 and FIG is written as 22. Using the same rule, how is TEAM written?
aptitude.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of the alphabet positions of its letters: B(2)+A(1)+D(4) = 7; F(6)+I(9)+G(7) = 22. TEAM = T(20)+E(5)+A(1)+M(13) = 39.

aptitude.question: P is the sister of Q. Q is the son of R. S is the only brother of R, and T is the wife of S. How is T related to P?
aptitude.explanation: Q is R's son and P is Q's sister, so P is R's child. S is R's brother, so S is P's uncle. T is S's wife, so T is P's aunt.

aptitude.question: Six packages P, Q, R, S, T and U are weighed. P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is heavier than R. T is lighter than Q. U is heavier than S. Which package is the third heaviest?
aptitude.explanation: Combining the clues: U > S > R > P > Q > T. The third heaviest is R.

aptitude.question: A warehouse starts the week with 1,250 units of a product. During the week it receives 3 shipments of 480 units each and dispatches 1,730 units to customers. What is the closing stock at the end of the week?
aptitude.explanation: Closing stock = opening + received - dispatched = 1,250 + (3 x 480) - 1,730 = 1,250 + 1,440 - 1,730 = 960 units.

aptitude.question: A technician is paid Rs. 180 per hour on weekdays, 1.25 times that rate on Saturdays and 2 times that rate on Sundays. In one week the technician works 40 weekday hours, 6 Saturday hours and 4 Sunday hours. What is the total pay for the week?
A company converts EUR 4,000 into rupees at 1 EUR = Rs. 90.50. From this amount it pays a supplier invoice of USD 3,500, converted at 1 USD = Rs. 83.00. How many rupees remain after the payment?
The table shows customer complaints received by category in two quarters. What percentage of all Q1 complaints were due to delivery delay?
aptitude.explanation: Total Q1 complaints = 120 + 80 + 60 + 40 + 20 = 320. Delivery delay share = 120/320 x 100 = 37.5%.

aptitude.question: The table shows customer complaints received by category in two quarters. Which category showed the largest percentage decrease in complaints from Q1 to Q2?
aptitude.explanation: Changes: Delivery delay 120->90 = -25%; Billing error 60->48 = -20%; Wrong item 40->35 = -12.5%; Damaged product and Other increased. The largest decrease is Delivery delay.

aptitude.question: The table shows customer complaints received by category in two quarters. What is the ratio of total damaged-product complaints to total billing-error complaints across both quarters combined?
aptitude.explanation: Damaged product = 80 + 100 = 180. Billing error = 60 + 48 = 108. Ratio = 180 : 108 = 5 : 3.

communication.question: Describe a project or assignment you worked on that did not go as planned. What went wrong, how did you respond at the time, and what specific lessons did you take from the experience into later work?
Tell us about a time you had to make a decision without having all the information you would have liked. How did you weigh the options and risks, what did you decide, and how did it turn out?

Sometimes a task must be delivered quickly but also to a high standard. Describe how you balance quality with speed, using an example where you had to decide what to prioritise and how you ensured the final result was acceptable.

Describe how you built a good working relationship with a new team, colleague or client. What did you do in the first few interactions to earn their trust, and how did that relationship help the work?

Workplaces often involve frequent interruptions such as calls, messages and unplanned requests. Explain how you handle interruptions and distractions while still completing your planned work on time, with a practical example.

Imagine you are asked to present your team's progress, including a problem the team is facing, to senior management. How would you prepare, how would you communicate the problem honestly, and how would you represent your team's efforts fairly?

Describe an occasion when you went beyond your assigned responsibilities at work, in a project or during your studies. What prompted you to do it, what exactly did you do, and what difference did it make?

You notice that one member of your team is consistently not contributing their fair share, and deadlines are at risk. Explain how you would address the situation with the colleague and the team while keeping the working relationship professional.

Describe a time you used a technology, tool or software to improve the way you or your team worked. What problem were you trying to solve, how did you learn and introduce the tool, and what measurable improvement resulted?

How do you measure your own performance at work or in your studies? Explain the indicators or feedback you rely on, how often you review your progress, and one change you made as a result of such a review.
